subject: Follow-up: streaming & concurrency qualification for ClearCart pilot
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearcart.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + numbers from today's discovery

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from ClearCart's side and a few numbers so you have concrete targets for qualification: 

- Primary UX requirement: token-level streaming so shoppers see partial responses while the model is generating (typeahead-style). Goal is perceived latency < 300ms for first tokens; token emission pacing ideally < 60ms/token for 95th percentile.
- End-to-end p95 (time-to-first-byte + first chunk): target <= 800ms for product-recommendation snippets (~30-80 tokens).
- Throughput: baseline expected sustained traffic ~150 req/s, with peak bursts to ~420 req/s during flash sales.
- Concurrency: ~1,200 concurrent active sessions at peak; average session = 4 requests/minute.
- Multi-turn behaviour: we expect KV/cache reuse across a session (same shopper), with average context length ~1.5k tokens and occasional extended sessions up to 6k tokens.

Questions we flagged for Redwood:
1) Can you support streaming with per-token latency targets above at scale? Any constraints for continuous batching?
2) What concurrency per-GPU do you recommend for these models to keep end-to-end p95 within target?
3) What cost levers (quantization, caching, model variants) would you recommend as tradeoffs?

I've attached our internal SLO workbook (see attachment). We'd like Redwood to propose two options: "latency-first" and "cost-optimized" with rough monthly estimates. Let's schedule a 60m follow-up workshop next week to walk the workbook with your infra folks.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Product
ClearCart

Attachment: clearcart_slo_workbook.xlsx (xlsx)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@clearcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T12:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + numbers from today's discovery

Samira — thanks for the clear numbers, very helpful. High-level responses inline and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Streaming & token latency: yes, we can support streaming with <60ms token emission for many model variants using our optimized runtime and low-batching paths. The main tradeoff is throughput efficiency — very small batching increases per-token compute cost.
- Concurrency per GPU: for a quantized 2B-6B family model with streaming enabled, practical concurrency per A100-style GPU is in the 60–120 concurrent streams range depending on batch strategy; for 7B+ models concurrent streams drop. We'll propose both Dedicated and Hosted sizing.
- Cost levers: continuous batching, prefix/KV caching across session turns, and int8/q4 quantization profiles are the strongest levers. Also model variants (distilled / lower-parameter families) and early-stopping heuristics for long responses.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) We'll produce two rough cost/SLAs: Latency-first (pin to high-perf model + conservative autoscale) and Cost-optimized (smaller model + aggressive batching + caching). Expect these by EOD tomorrow; attaching Redwood proposal v2.
2) Book a 60m workshop with infra + engineering: we'll bring karthik (serving lead) and marissa (SRE/ops). Please propose 3 slots.
3) Can you send a small sample of typical prompts (5 examples) and a traffic profile CSV (qps by minute for a 2-hour flash event)? That will let us simulate batching and tail behavior.

Notes on immediate feasibility and concerns:
- Continuous batching: will help cost but increases latency SLO risk for the first token unless we maintain low-latency fast-paths for 5–10% of traffic (we can mark high-priority routes).
- KV cache: obvious win for multi-turn; need session affinity (sticky routing) or shared external cache. We'll layout options in the workbook.

I'll follow up with the cost sketches and a proposed agenda for the workshop.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: sizing notes for ClearCart (for workshop)

Quick internal note before the workshop. Based on Samira's numbers and a short spike model, my rough recommendations:

- Option A (Latency-first):
  - Model: redwood-2-large (7B) quantized to q4f16 for lower mem while preserving perf.
  - Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool (A100/80GB-equivalent), autoscale to sustain 420 rps bursts.
  - Concurrency: assume 40–60 streaming streams per GPU for 7B family to keep p95 start <800ms.
  - Caching: session KV + prefix caching for repeated prompt-sequences (expected 25–35% token savings).
  - Cost: higher baseline (estimate included in workbook).

- Option B (Cost-optimized):
  - Model: redwood-2-medium or a distilled 3B family quantized to int8 where possible.
  - Deployment: consolidated Dedicated with aggressive continuous batching and larger burst capacity triggers.
  - Concurrency: 100–160 concurrent streams per GPU projected for 3B family with batching; p95 will be higher but still possibly within 1.2s E2E.
  - Caching + early-stop heuristics: critical to keep token spend down.

Operational notes:
- Session affinity: recommend sticky routing for KV reuse. Without sticky routing we can provide a shared cache layer but that adds networking overhead.
- Canary: roll a canary on 10% traffic using latency-first profile, measure token-emission-rate and tail latencies, then shift traffic.

I'll prepare a one-slide SLO-vs-cost table plus the rough monthly estimate to bring to the workshop.

— karthik
Lead, Serving Runtime

Also, can Redwood provide a short note on recommended quantization profiles (int8 vs q4f16) and expected quality delta for the recommended models? Even bullet points are fine.

We'll confirm the workshop slot and send the prompts + CSV shortly. Looking forward to the runbook + estimates.

Best,
